description_en: With its historicity dating back to the mid-17th century, Ināco Bāhāḥ has a monastic association (saṃgha) of the Buddhācāryas.Located in Bhaktapur's Inācoṭola, the three-storiedbāhāḥfacing west has a balconied tower (phucā) on top of its roof of corrugated metal sheets. Five struts are placed to support the load of the roof. A metal ornamented arch (toraṇa) is placed under the window of the second floor. Two statues placed in the upper part of thetoraṇahave been stolen. The esoteric room (āgaṃ) has been established on the first floor of thebāhāḥ. On this floor, there is a gilded window with a row of five openings (pasukājhyāḥ). Thepasukājhyāḥis flanked by European-styled icons of women. On the ground floor of the monastic building (dyaḥchẽ) lies the main sanctum of thebāhāḥ. The entrance to the sanctum is covered with brass sheets. A metaltoraṇawith a statue of Akṣobhya at the center is placed on top of the entrance. Murals of Rāma and Rāvaṇa are painted on the wall on either side of the door. Threecaityas are established in thebāhāḥ's courtyard.The existence of thisbāhāḥis historically seen only from the later-medieval period. Scholars who have researched thebāhāḥmention that it was established in 1621 CE (NS 741) during the reign of King Jagajyoti Malla. S. Śākya (1120, p.30-31) writes that Devasiṃha Buddhācārya, Jayasiṃha Buddhācārya, Muni Buddhācārya, and Kuśala Buddhācārya jointly founded the bāhāḥ in 1621 CE (NS 741) during the reign of King Jagajyoti Malla. B. Vajrācārya (1124, p.38) has written that Devasiṃha Buddhācārya, Jayasiṃha Buddhācārya, Melusiṃ Buddhācārya bought a plot of land on the 9th of the dark fortnight of Kārtika in 1621 CE (NS 741) during the reign of King Jagajyoti Malla and established thebāhāḥ. They claim to possess a palm-leaf document from NS 741 that records the event. However, the study of the land deed does not prove that the land was purchased for the construction of thebāhāḥin NS 741 as claimed by them. This palm-leaf document is in the private collection of Indrarāja Śākya, one of the elders (āḥju) of thebāhāḥ. B. Vajrācārya (1124, p.141, appendix no. 65) has published the original text of the palm-leaf, which only records the purchase of land by Devasiṃha Buddhācārya (text: Budhācāryya Devasiṃha); it does not mention that the land was bought for thebāhāḥor that thebāhāḥwas built on the land. Apart from the name of Devasiṃha Buddhācārya, the other names do not feature in the document. Thebāhāḥmembers were unwilling to show the original copy of the palm-leaf document.Thebāhāḥis comprised of asaṃghaof the Buddhācārya caste. Although a Buddhācārya, some members write Śākya as their caste. They claim that their ancestors came from Taḥchẽ Bāhāḥ (KAT0470) of Kathmandu and are proud to be the descendants of Suratavajra (B. Vajrācārya 1124, p.39). The patron deity (digudyaḥ) of thebāhāḥmembers is Guhyeśvarī in Kathmandu but has now been ‘pulled’ by the means of tantric practice and enshrined at Siddhapokhari in Bhaktapur (S. Śākya 1120, p.30).Thebāhāḥmembers have spread to Palpa and Darjeeling. Earlier, they used to come from there to Bhaktapur to perform the initiation of their boys (barechuigu), but have ceased to do so. The members ofbāhāḥare performing daily rituals by taking a turn for one month each. Every year, the alms-giving (pañcadāna) festival is organized on the 14th of the dark fortnight of Bhādra. Alms are also given to the five portable statues of Dīpaṅkara of Bhaktapur. Throughout the holy month of Guṃlā (July-August), devotional verses (stotra) are recited at thebāhāḥin the evening.
description_ne: नेसं ७६३ (सन् १६४३) देखि प्रामाणिक रूपले अस्तित्वमा देखिने यस बाहाःमा बुद्धाचार्यहरूको संघ रहेको छ ।भक्तपुरको इनाचो टोलमा रहेको यो बाहाःको द्यःछेँ पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी तीन तलाको बनाइएको छ । द्यःछेँको छानामा जस्तापाता राखिएको छ । छानाको भार थाम्न पाँचवटा टुँडालहरू राखिएका छन् । छानामा फुचा पनि राखिएको छ । दोस्रो तलाको झ्यालमुनि धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । तोरणको माथिल्लो भागमा राखिएका दुईवटा मूर्तिहरू चोरी भइसकेका छन् । द्यःछेँको पहिलो तलामा आगम स्थापना गरिएको छ । यस तलामा सुनको मोलम्बा लगाइएकोपसुकाझ्याःराखिएको छ ।पसुकाझ्याःको दायाँबायाँ यूरोपेली शैलीका कन्याहरू राखिएका छन् । द्यःछेँको भुइँतलामा बाहाःको गर्भगृह रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामा पित्तलको पाताले मोडिएको छ । ढोकामाथि अक्षोभ्य अङ्कित धातुको तोरण राखिएको छ । ढोकाको उत्तरपट्टि भित्तामा राम र दक्षिणपट्टि भित्तामा रावणका चित्रहरू कोरिएका छन् । बाहाः प्राङ्गणमा तीनवटा चैत्य स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।प्रामाणिक रूपले उत्तरमध्यकालदेखि मात्र यस बाहाःको अस्तित्व भेटिन्छ । यस बाहाःसम्बन्धी अध्ययन गरेका पूर्वअध्येयताहरूले राजा जगज्योति मल्लको राज्यकालमा नेसं ७४१ (सन् १६२१) मा बाहाः स्थापना गरिएको कुरा लेखेका छन् । S. Śākya (1120, p.30-31) ले देवसिंह बुद्धाचार्य, जयसिंह बुद्धाचार्य, मुनी बुद्धाचार्य र कुशल बुद्धाचार्यले मिलेर राजा जगज्योति मल्लको राज्यकालमा नेसं ७४१ (सन् १६२१) मा बाहाः स्थापना गरेको कुरा लेखेका छन् । B. Vajrācārya (1124, p.38) ले देवसिंह बुद्धाचार्य, जयसिंह बुद्धाचार्य, मेलुसिं बुद्धाचार्यले राजा जगज्योति मल्लको राज्यकालमा नेसं ७४१ कार्तिक कृष्ण ९ (सन् १६२१) मा जग्गा किनेर बाहाः स्थापना गरेको कुरा लेखेका छन् । यस कुराको पुष्टि गर्ने उनीहरूले नेसं ७४१ को ताडपत्रलाई प्रमाणको रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् । तर उक्त ताडपत्रको अध्ययनपछि उनीहरूले दावी गरे जस्तो नेसं ७४१ मा जग्गा किनी बाहाः निर्माण गरिएको कुरा प्रमाणित हुँदैन । यो ताडपत्र बाहाःका आःजु इन्द्रराज शाक्यको संग्रहमा रहेको छ । S. Śākya (1120, p.85) ले ताडपत्रको मूलपाठ छापेका छैनन् । B. Vajrācārya (1124, p.141, appendix no. 65) ले ताडपत्रको मूलपाठ छापेका छन् । उक्त ताडपत्रको मूलपाठमा बुधाचार्य्य देवसिंहले जग्गा किनेको कुरा मात्र लेखिएको छ, बाहाःको लागि जग्गा किनिएको वा त्यस जग्गामा बाहाः बनाइएको भन्ने कुरा लेखिएको छैन । ताडपत्रमा देवसिंह बुद्धाचार्य्य बाहेक अन्य अंशियारहरूको नाम पनि लेखिएको छैन । बाहाःका संघ सदस्यहरूले ताडपत्रको मूल प्रति देखाउन चाहेनन् । प्रामाणिक रूपले नेसं ७६३ (सन् १६४३) देखि यो बाहाःको अस्तित्व देखिन्छ । उक्त मितिमा देव बुद्धाचार्य, जय बुद्धाचार्य, मुनि बुद्धाचार्य र रथन बुद्धाचार्यले मिलेर आगमदेवता स्थापना गरेका थिए (S. Śākya1120, p.32; B. Vajrācārya 1124, p.141) । बाहाःमा स्थापना गरिएका चैत्यहरू शाहकालीन हुन् ।यस बाहाःमा बुद्धाचार्यहरूको संघ रहेको छ । बुद्धाचार्य भएपनि कतिपयले शाक्य पनि लेख्ने गरेका छन् । उनीहरू आफ्ना पुर्खाहरू काठमाडौको तःछेँ बाहाः (KAT0470) बाट आएको दावी गर्छन् र आफूहरू सुरतवज्रका सन्तान भएकोमा गर्व गर्छन् (B. Vajrācārya 1124, p.39) । यहाँका संघ सदस्यहरूको दिगुद्यः काठमाडौंमा रहेको गुह्येश्वरी हो, तर अहिले साधना गरेर भक्तपुरको सिद्धपोखरीमा सारिएको छ (S. Śākya1120, p.30) । यहाँका संघ सदस्यहरू पाल्पा र दार्जिलिङसम्म पनि फैलिएका छन् । पहिले त त्यहाँबाट भक्तपुरसम्म आएरबरे छुइगुसंस्कार गर्न आउँथे, अहिले भने आउन छोडेका छन् । बाहाःका संघ सदस्यहरूले एक-एक महिनाको पालो मिलाएर नित्यपूजा गरिरहेका छन् । प्रत्येक वर्षजुगःचःह्रय्(भाद्र शुक्ल १३) को दिनमा बाहाःमा पञ्चदानको आयोजना गरिन्छ । भक्तपुरका पाँचजना दीपङ्करलाई पनि दान प्रदान गरिन्छ । नेपाल सम्वत्‌अनुसार गुंला महिनाभरि बिहान बाजा बजाएर भक्तपुर शहर परिक्रमा गरिन्छ र बेलुकी बाहाःमा स्तोत्र वाचन गरिन्छ ।
references: Sources and references Sources Palmleaf document from NS 763 in possession of Sureśajyoti Śakya. See, S. Śākya 1120, p.32; for full text, see, B. Vajrācārya 1124, p.141. S. Śākya (1120, p.85) has published the facsimile of the document in appendix.

historical_events.event_description: Deva Buddhācārya, Jaya Buddhācārya, Muni Buddhācārya, and Rathana Buddhācārya jointly established the esoteric deity (āgaṃdyaḥ).
During the reign of King Pṛthvī Vikrama Śāha, Budhacāryya Jayanarasiṃ, his wife Mayjulāni, and son Bekhāmuni established adharmadhātujinālayacaitya(BKT0320-005) in thebāhāḥ's courtyard.
Four brothers Budhācāryya Amoghavajra, Jñā(na)vajra, Māhāvajra, and Paṃcarāja offered a bell (BKT0320-008).
Harṣa Budhācārje, together with his mother and son, offered a brass door for the sanctum, wishing for the heavenly abode of Sukhāvati Bhuvana for his deceased father Haṣamāna.

Maṃjumuni and his family members established acaityain the name of his deceased parents Amṛtamuni and Lataṃ Thakuṃ. They also endowed land to observe the anniversary ritual of thecaitya. It is not clear which of thecaityas at thebāhāḥis being referred to here.

Budhācārje Sākebhikṣu Bekhāmuni, the seniormost elder (thapāḥju) of thebāhāḥ, endowed oneropanīof land to continue the tradition of playing musical instruments throughout the holy month of Guṃlā (July-August).

historical_events.event_name: Replacement of jhĩgaṭī tiles with brass sheets
historical_events.event_description: Putali Thakuṃ, his son Harṣavajra and others replaced the traditional tiles on the roof of thebāhāḥ’s balconied tower (phucā) with brass sheets. They also covered the struts and other parts of thephucāwith brass sheets. The names of Mahāvaja, Paṃcarāja, Mohanamāyā, Visnumāyā, and others are engraved on the lower part of the struts.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a pair of metal flags and prayer wheels
historical_events.event_description: Śākebhikṣu Jñānavajra vowed to offer a pair of brass flags and 10 copper prayer wheels. As he passed away before he could fulfill his vow, his wife Putalimāyā and her family members including son Sugatarājā offered flags and prayer wheels as per the vow of her late husband.

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of a pair of metal lions (BKT0320-002 and BKT0320-003)
historical_events.event_description: Maṃjumuni and his family members offered a pair of metal lions (BKT0320-002 and BKT0320-003).
Budhācājye Amokavajra, Gyanavajra, and Māhāvajra jointly offered a gilded ornamented arch (toraṇa) over the entrance to the sanctum of thebāhāḥ.
The earthquake caused some damage to thephucāon the roof of thebāhāḥ. Although thephucādid not collapse, it was displaced. Thebāhāḥ's members carried out minor repairs to thephucā.
